data.value: Installs into the Blueprint Loader's folders rather than this app's own. Useful for proving a payload works against a loader somebody else has already debugged, which keeps "did my level cook correctly" and "does my bootstrap work" as two questions rather than one.

data.name: MODS_INSTALL_PAYLOAD_WHY
data.value: Installs something cooked in Unreal - a level with blueprints, lights or models in it - into the folder a blueprint loader watches, so the game runs it at the chosen moment. The menu beside this says when, and Menu is usually the right answer: the main menu is a rendered camp scene, so anything loaded there is created first and stays for the whole session - in the Camp and in missions alike. Lobby and Ingame are for things that should exist only at that moment. Authoring one needs the editor; this only moves it into place.

data.comment: After the jump key is pressed

data.name: ESCALATION_EVERY_WHY
data.value: How long before everything gets worse. A minute is a starting point rather than a finding - somebody who clears a level in four minutes and somebody who searches it for twenty want very different numbers here.

data.name: ESCALATION_TOUGH_STEP_WHY
data.value: What each stage adds to how much punishment enemies take. Zero leaves toughness out of the ramp entirely.
data.comment: Why the toughness step is adjustable

data.name: ESCALATION_SPEED_STEP_WHY
data.value: And to how fast they move, which wants a much smaller number. Toughness at ten times is a fight that takes ten times as long; speed at ten times is not a fight at all, because they cross the room faster than the camera turns. Zero leaves speed alone.
data.comment: Why the speed step is smaller

data.name: ESCALATION_MOST_TOUGH_WHY
data.value: Where toughness stops climbing. Ten times is a tenth of your damage landing, which is slow rather than impossible.

data.name: ESCALATION_MOST_SPEED_WHY
data.value: Where speed stops climbing. Three times is about as fast as an enemy can be and still be something you can back away from. Wind it up if you want the version where the level eventually wins.

data.name: ESCALATION_ON
data.value: Enemies get worse the longer you stay

data.name: ESCALATION_WHY
data.value: Every minute in a level adds 0.2 to how tough and how fast the enemies are, stopping at ten times tough and three times fast. The sliders above become where the ramp starts rather than what is written. A bar over the game says which stage you are in and how long until the next one. The clock restarts when you load into a new level, and not when you die.

data.name: ESCALATION_STAGE
data.comment: Stage number and name on the overlay

data.name: ESCALATION_TOPPED

data.name: STATS_ENEMY_JUMP
data.value: J throws every enemy into the air

data.name: STATS_ENEMY_JUMP_WHY
data.value: Press J while the game has the keyboard and every enemy in the level is launched upwards. It is what makes the gravity slider visible: a mob that walks never leaves the ground, so how heavily it would fall changes nothing until something puts it up there. Ten launched at the same strength reached 143 units at normal gravity, 1440 at a tenth and 2996 at a fortieth.
data.comment: Why the enemy jump key exists

data.name: STATS_ENEMY_JUMP_POWER
data.comment: Caption for the enemy jump strength

data.name: STATS_ENEMY_JUMP_POWER_WHY
data.value: How hard J throws them. Written as a launch the movement component picks up on its next tick, which is the same way your own Q jump works.
data.comment: Why the jump strength slider exists

data.name: STATS_ENEMY_GRAVITY
data.comment: Caption for the enemy gravity slider

data.name: STATS_ENEMY_GRAVITY_WHY
data.value: How heavily enemies fall, as a multiple of their own weight. Written straight onto each creature's movement, the same number the mount uses to take a creature's weight away - so a mob knocked into the air at a fortieth of its weight keeps going up. Knockback weapons and the Wind Horn become launchers. Their own weight is remembered, because a creature that floats or falls heavily by design does so through this number.
data.comment: Why the enemy gravity slider exists

data.name: WEAPON_SKINS_GLOW_HINT
data.value: Turns up the emissive the material already carries - the same numbers that make the Torment arrow glow blue, which sits at 125. Nothing is added: a material with no emissive value cannot be lit this way, and says so after applying.

data.name: WEAPON_SKINS_SCOPE
data.value: Melee weapons and the things the game throws. Bows change shape as they are drawn, and armour is several pieces that have to match, so neither is here yet.

data.name: WEAPON_SKINS_BOW_CAUTION
data.value: A bow is four meshes - the shapes it takes as the string is pulled - and your model goes into all four. So it stops bending as it is drawn: the draw animation is still played, but every frame of it is the same shape. Arrange it against this one and the other three follow.

data.name: WEAPON_SKINS_NO_COLOUR

data.comment: Shown when an imported model has no artwork

data.name: WEAPON_SKINS_BOW_NOTE
data.value: Only the first draw state of each bow is listed. Your model is written into all of them when you apply, so the weapon looks the same drawn as it does at rest.
data.comment: Under the list when bows are shown

data.name: WEAPON_SKINS_PROJECTILE_NOTE
data.value: A projectile flies along its own length, so a model whose nose points somewhere else will fly sideways - turn it with the sliders until it does. The ordinary arrow is shared by every bow, so changing it changes them all.
data.comment: Shown against every projectile in the list

data.name: WEAPON_SKINS_MELEE_ONLY

data.comment: Why ranged and armour are absent

data.comment: bUsePawnControlRotation - the one that actually makes a following camera

data.name: CAMERA_FOLLOWS_AIM_HINT
data.value: Takes the camera's angle straight from your aim. The pitch comes from the aim too, and this game's aim pitch jumps rather than sweeps, so expect the view to swing.

data.name: CAMERA_AIM_ALREADY_ON
data.value: Your character already turns to face aim in this game, so that setting changes nothing here. It is written for the pak, where it still matters.
data.comment: Explains why the face-aim checkbox looks inert

data.name: CAMERA_MOUSE_LOOK
data.value: Turn the camera with the mouse

data.name: CAMERA_MOUSE_LOOK_HINT
data.value: Pins the pointer to the middle of the game window, so moving the mouse turns the view and your character aims at whatever you are looking at. Opening any menu hands the pointer back on its own, and closing it takes it again - the game is asked directly rather than guessed at. Alt tab frees it too, and F10 turns everything off from inside the game. Clicking away from the game frees it too.
data.comment: Explains mouse look and how to escape it

data.name: CAMERA_WASD
data.value: Move with W A S D

data.name: CAMERA_WASD_HINT
data.value: Walks relative to the camera, so W is always away from you. Hold Ctrl to walk slowly - Shift is left alone, because the game uses it to plant your feet so you can swing at something out of reach. This game has no movement keys of its own, so the input is written straight into the game - there is no virtual controller, which is what used to cost frames.

data.name: CAMERA_BUTTONS
data.comment: Checkbox - remaps the mouse buttons to the attack keys

data.name: CAMERA_BUTTONS_HINT
data.value: This game binds a left click to two things at once: attack, and walk to where you clicked. With the keys moving you, the second one fights them. The click still swings - melee needs the cursor to know what it is hitting - but where it told you to walk is thrown away. Needs W A S D switched on.

data.name: CAMERA_THIRD_PERSON
data.comment: Button - turns everything on at once

data.name: CAMERA_THIRD_PERSON_HINT
data.value: One switch for all of it: the camera comes in behind your character, and mouse look, W A S D and the clicking all turn on together. F10 works from inside the game, which matters because the pointer is pinned while this is on. Turning it off puts the camera back. Every switch below still works on its own.

data.name: CAMERA_SUSPENDED
data.value: Menu open - the pointer is yours. It comes back on its own when you close it.
data.comment: Shown while mouse look is suspended

data.name: CAMERA_PIVOT
data.comment: How far up the character the camera orbits and looks

data.name: CAMERA_SAVE_HINT
data.value: Adjust the sliders, then give it a name to keep it. Saved presets appear in the list above and come back in one click.

data.name: CAMERA_SAVE_BUILT_IN
data.value: That name belongs to one of the presets that ship. Pick another.

data.value: {0} - adjust anything below and it changes in the game as you drag.

data.name: CAMERA_RESTORED
data.value: The game's own camera is back.

data.name: ENEMIES_RESTORE
data.comment: Button - restores the level's own numbers

data.name: ENEMIES_HINT
data.value: Multiplies what the level's own spawners were told to send. Nothing is written to disk and nothing is injected - quitting the game puts it all back. It follows you into a new level, because each one brings its own spawners.

data.name: ENEMIES_NONE_HERE
data.value: No wave spawners here. The camp has almost none - load into a mission to see what this does.
data.comment: Status when the level has no spawners

data.name: ENEMIES_COUNT_WHY
data.value: Multiplies every wave's size - where it starts, how much it grows and where it stops. Three is a noticeably busier fight; eight is a swarm.

data.name: ENEMIES_RATE_WHY
data.value: How quickly waves arrive. Higher means less breathing room between them, which stacks with the count rather than replacing it.

data.name: ENEMIES_SPREAD_WHY
data.value: The radius a spawner scatters its wave across. Wider surrounds you; narrower drops them in a clump you can meet head on.

data.name: ENEMIES_CLOSENESS_WHY
data.value: How near you they are allowed to appear. Lower gets ambushes, higher gives you the moment to see them coming that the level intended.

data.name: STATS_HINT
data.value: Applied to the running game and held there, because enemies that appear later are built fresh. Nothing is written to disk - quitting the game puts everything back, and so does the button.

data.name: STATS_NO_CHARACTER
data.value: Waiting for a character - load into the camp or a mission.

data.name: STATS_PLAYER_BACK
data.value: Your character is back to normal.

data.name: STATS_TOUGH_WHY
data.value: How many hits they take to kill. This changes the damage they take rather than the health they have, which is the same thing to play against and does not care what kind of enemy it is.

data.name: STATS_ENEMY_SPEED_WHY
data.value: How quickly they close on you. Small changes here are felt more than large ones anywhere else - a slow enemy you can walk away from is a different enemy at 1.5x.

data.name: STATS_YOUR_SPEED_WHY
data.value: How fast you move, on top of whatever your gear already gives you.

data.name: STATS_DODGE_COOLDOWN_WHY
data.value: Seconds between rolls. The game gives you 2.5.

data.name: STATS_DODGE_CHARGES_WHY
data.value: How many rolls you can chain before waiting. The game gives you one.

data.name: STATS_GRAVITY_WHY
data.value: How heavily you fall. Lower makes every gap and ledge more forgiving.

data.name: STATS_ATTACK_SPEED_WHY
data.value: How fast you swing and shoot. Applied to both your melee and your ranged weapon, since nobody wants half of it.

data.name: STATS_RENDER_WHY
data.value: Third person costs frames for a reason that has nothing to do with this app: looking along a corridor puts far more enemies on screen than looking down at the floor, and each one is a skeleton being posed, drawn and casting a shadow. These make a crowd cheaper without making it smaller.

data.name: STATS_POSE_WHEN_SEEN
data.value: Only animate what you can see

data.name: STATS_DRAW_DISTANCE_WHY
data.value: How far away an enemy is still drawn, in centimetres. All the way up means never stop, which is what the game does.

data.name: STATS_RENDER_BACK
data.value: Enemies are drawn the way the game draws them again.

data.name: STATS_POSE_WHY
data.value: The game animates every enemy in the level every frame, including the ones behind you. Unreal has a setting for not doing that and this game does not use it. Measured at 54 frames a second before and 138 after, in a fight with 198 enemies. It changes nothing you can see.

data.name: CAMERA_JUMP_WHY
data.value: The game has no jump at all. This one is not the character jumping but a launch written straight into its velocity, which is why it works when asking the character nicely does not. On Q rather than space, because a jump that also rolls is harder to aim and harder to stop doing by accident. Needs W A S D switched on.

data.name: CAMERA_CROSSHAIR
data.comment: Caption for the crosshair style and colour

data.name: CAMERA_SMOOTHING
data.comment: Slider for how rigidly the camera follows the character

data.name: CAMERA_FORWARD
data.comment: Slider for how far in front of the face the camera sits

data.name: MOUNT_WHY
data.value: Press R once to get on, again to get off. Nothing here spawns anything, but the game does: any summoning artifact - Enchanted Grass, Tasty Bone, Golem Kit, Wonderful Wheat - drops a creature beside you, and it does not have to be there when you press R. With nothing underneath you it keeps looking, and climbs onto the first creature that comes within reach. Needs W A S D switched on.

data.name: MOUNT_FOUND_NONE
data.value: Nothing nearby that walks. Ride still works - it will just be speed.

data.name: FLY_WHY
data.value: Press G in game to take off and again to land. Space climbs and C drops; forward goes wherever the camera is pointed, so look down to dive. Gravity is off while flying, which is what holds you up - there is no way to hold a walking character in the air from outside. Needs W A S D switched on.

data.name: BOARD_WHY
data.value: Takes whatever is in your hand off your arm and puts it flat under your feet. Pack a model over the Mace on the Weapon Skins tab first and it becomes a skateboard; without that it is whatever you happen to be holding, lying on the floor.

data.name: BOARD_HEIGHT

data.comment: Says how many held meshes were found

data.name: BOARD_FOUND_NONE
data.value: Nothing equipped that could be a board.

data.name: MOUNT_TAB_INTRO
data.value: Nothing here spawns anything - spawning is a function call, and this app only writes memory. The Totem of Regeneration does spawn, though: the artifact drops a rigid object on the floor wherever you stand. Replace what that object looks like, and it is your mount.

data.name: MOUNT_TAB_BOARD
